key_insight: Auditing automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems is most effective when driven by the people affected: a stakeholder-centered audit uncovers real-world harms and priorities that purely technical tests miss, leading to more actionable, equitable evaluations.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between standard benchmark evaluations and the lived needs and harms experienced by diverse ASR users — including dialects, accents, disability-related speech, and contextual misuse — by making audits inclusive, contextualized, and actionable.
method: Define and engage diverse stakeholders (end users, affected communities, domain experts, deployers) to co-design audit goals and success criteria.

Combine quantitative disaggregated testing (accuracy/error analyses by demographic, dialect, environment) with qualitative methods (interviews, contextual harm assessments) to surface harms and priorities.
Produce transparent, repeatable audit protocols and remediation cycles (reporting, policy recommendations, iterative model or data changes) tied to stakeholder-defined metrics.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical roadmap to evaluate ASR beyond aggregate metrics, improving fairness, reliability, compliance, and user trust by centering those who experience system failures.
visual_elements: Flowchart of a stakeholder-driven audit loop: stakeholder input → co-designed metrics → mixed-method evaluation → remediation → re-audit
Bar or heatmap showing disaggregated ASR error rates across accents/dialects and environments (before vs after remediation)
Stakeholder map iconography (users, clinicians, developers, regulators) with arrows illustrating roles and inputs
Audit checklist/dashboard mockup summarizing quantitative metrics, qualitative findings, and recommended actions
paper_title: The case for stakeholder-driven AI auditing in automatic speech recognition
paper_authors: Mona Sloane, Hilke Schellmann, Katelyn Xiaoying Mei, Anna Seo Gyeong Choi, Allison Koenecke
